# Research-preview governance

Reviewed: 2026-08-02. Applies to the publisher-source research preview only.

## Responsibility and review method

The repository owner `TheDarkniteFalls` is the review owner. A record may enter
the preview only after the maintainer checks the exact product surface and
channel, publisher identity, source ownership, release identity, applicability,
claim wording, unknowns, lifecycle links, independent-evidence admission, and
public-safety boundary. Deterministic validation is necessary but not a truth
or publication decision.

The maintainer records a source-only dossier before generating a record,
mapping, lifecycle entry, watcher applicability, or page. A second source may
corroborate identity, but claims do not transfer between versions, models,
configurations, channels or related product surfaces. A public correction or
new source reopens the affected review; it does not modify a record
automatically.

## Identity, correction, dispute and appeal

- Publisher identity must be supported by a publisher-controlled domain,
  official repository, official registry account, or release-signing identity.
  Similar names and third-party package listings are insufficient.
- A factual correction identifies the exact record, claim, source and proposed
  bounded change. Public-safe corrections may use a public issue or pull request
  only after the repository is published.
- A dispute records the claimant's position separately from the maintainer's
  evidence decision. Disagreement does not silently delete provenance or alter
  another surface.
- An appeal must supply new public evidence, a demonstrated scope error, or a
  documented process error. The maintainer gives a reasoned public-safe
  decision when practical. No response or resolution time is promised.
- Sensitive material follows `SECURITY.md`; it must never be posted publicly.

## Publisher contact

Publishers do not receive approval authority over catalog inclusion, wording or
timing. The maintainer may seek a factual clarification only under separate
authorization, with the question and resulting public evidence recorded. The
preview makes no promise of pre-publication notice, reply, correction or
embargo handling. No publisher was contacted for this candidate.

## Evidence handling

Use the smallest public evidence necessary: source URL, title, locator,
timestamp, digest when defensible, neutral claim, applicability, limitations
and unknowns. Do not copy full articles, proprietary documentation, credentials,
personal data, unpublished material, private reports, exploit payloads or raw
environment logs.

Repository-authored records are Apache-2.0. Linked third-party source material,
product names and trademarks retain their owners' rights and are not relicensed.
If a source is withdrawn or becomes inaccessible, keep only public-safe
provenance needed to explain history, remove unsupported claims from the active
view through an explicit revision, and retain the lifecycle event. A rights or
privacy request may require removal of material from the working tree; Git
history is not promised as a retention mechanism for content that should not
remain public.

## Security-sensitive detail

If evidence would enable exploitation, credential misuse, bypass or targeting,
the public record states only the minimum non-actionable boundary and marks the
detail withheld. Sensitive detail may be reviewed only through an operational
private route. Until that route exists, sensitive material is not accepted and
the affected claim or record is withheld. This limitation does not block the
static preview as a whole while it contains only public publisher sources and
keeps intake closed. The private route is tracked in `ROADMAP.md`.

## Names, marks and affiliation

Use publishers' public product names only to identify the researched surface.
Do not use logos without a separate rights review. Do not imply sponsorship,
partnership, certification, endorsement or publisher approval. Inclusion is
not endorsement; absence is not an adverse finding.

## Freshness and lifecycle

- Fast-moving release feeds may be checked daily; rolling documentation is
  reviewed weekly or at its recorded cadence; security policy is reviewed
  quarterly.
- Every watcher change requires human applicability review. Fingerprints do not
  advance automatically.
- Revalidate after a new exact release, material rolling-source change,
  claimant correction, configuration change, source loss or manual review.
- Current, superseded, historical, discontinued and unresolved are distinct.
  Only direct same-surface links may supersede one another.
- An overdue review creates a visible gap; it does not manufacture a lifecycle
  transition. Removal and revocation remain explicit, reviewable actions.

## Configuration and artifact identity

Publisher-source records may identify exact release assets and publisher
digests without claiming an installed runtime. Effective model revision,
authentication, configuration, permissions, tools, credentials, runtime and
network state remain unresolved unless an admitted source pins them. Executed
artifact types and hashed effective configurations remain requirements of the
deferred evaluation layer, not fields to fabricate in this source-only preview.

## Curation, intake and conflicts

The research preview is maintainer-curated. Public intake, paid placement,
sponsorship ordering, voting and automated ingestion are closed. Any material
employment, investment, sponsorship, publisher or competitor relationship
relevant to a record must be disclosed before that record is published or
reviewed by an unconflicted maintainer. This preview contains no sponsorship
placement and makes no claim that the maintainer is an independent evaluator.

Publisher statements, maintainer source-capture decisions and independent
evaluation are separate roles. The current preview contains publisher claims
and maintainer curation only; independent evaluators and independent tests are
empty throughout.
